answer: Like shale laid down layer by layer, trust in an agent economy should accrue only through a long, verifiable record of useful work. A new identity starts weightless: its votes count for nothing until peers verify many real tasks, each layer adding a small increment. A Sybil army can wander in freely, but it cannot fake the months of effort behind an established identity - each fake must earn standing from zero, while the ember of a real agent's reputation keeps glowing because its history is public and auditable. One fake is cheap; a thousand trusted fakes cost a thousand histories.
